title: Hat Yai Nightlife Plan: Greenway, Lee Gardens & Bar Streets | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: A walkable night plan for Hat Yai, Thailand — from Greenway Night Market to Lee Gardens, the night bazaar, and the bar streets around Niphat Uthit. With rough prices and honest safety tips for the evening.
keywords: Hat Yai nightlife, Lee Gardens night market, Greenway Hat Yai, Hat Yai bar street, Hat Yai bars
h1:
Hat Yai After Dark
Greenway, Lee Gardens & the Bar Streets
intro: What makes Hat Yai fun at night is that everything sits within walking distance — from the Greenway night market to Lee Gardens, the night bazaar, and the eat-and-drink streets around Niphat Uthit. You can start with street snacks, move on to a spot with live music, then close the night with late-night rice porridge, all in one evening. We've mapped it out by time slots so you can walk from one place to the next without backtracking, and we'll tell you straight where to keep your guard up.

blocks.html: The good thing about Hat Yai in the evening is that the lively areas cluster downtown in a loose triangle between Lee Gardens Plaza, the Greenway market, and the run of Niphat Uthit roads 1–3. Most hops from one to the next take no more than 10–15 minutes on foot, so you rarely need to hail a ride. We've laid the plan out as a run of time slots from early evening into the small hours, then split it into a family-friendly night and a chill night out so you can pick by mood.

blocks.text: The 3 main nightlife zones at a glance

blocks.html: Before the hour-by-hour plan, getting these three zones straight makes the whole trip far easier to organise. Each one has a clearly different mood.

items: Greenway Night Market — a craft-leaning night market with clean food stalls, live bands, and a more open feel than your average market. It runs roughly 17:00–22:00 and is geared toward strolling, snacking, and browsing handmade goods. Prices sit a touch above a regular street market, but the stalls are tidy and well organised.

Lee Gardens Night Market — right next to Lee Gardens Plaza Hotel. Once evening sets in, the road in front of the mall turns into a long market selling clothes, souvenirs, and roadside Thai street food. It's an easy starting point because the Lee Gardens tower is a landmark you can spot from a distance.

The Niphat Uthit 1–3 eat-and-drink area — the stretch of restaurants and bars that locals actually use, from late-night rice-porridge shops to a legendary spot that's been open 40 years on Niphat Uthit 3 Soi 1, all the way to pubs with live bands playing Thai songs. This is where Hat Yai people genuinely come out to sit.

blocks.title: How to hit it all
blocks.html: Start at Greenway early in the evening since it closes first (around 22:00), then drift over to Lee Gardens and Niphat Uthit, which run later into the night. That way you won't miss the market that shuts down earliest.

Eating in Hat Yai at night can go on for hours. We've picked out food you'll find around the markets and the eat-and-drink area from evening into the small hours, ordered from light walk-and-eat snacks to a heavier late-night meal. Prices are rough ranges based on what most stalls charge.

items.name: Salt-grilled fish (Greenway Market)
items.blurb: A whole fish packed in salt and grilled over flame, the flesh sweet and juicy. It's the dish people queue up for at Greenway, eaten with a punchy seafood dipping sauce and great for sharing.

items.name: Volcano pork bone soup
items.blurb: A hot pot of pork-bone soup served piled high like a volcano, with a rich, deep broth. It's one of Greenway's most photographed dishes and warms you up nicely.

items.name: Street food in front of Lee Gardens
items.blurb: The line of carts and stalls in front of Lee Gardens — grilled pork skewers, roti, deep-fried snacks, and fresh juice. Easy to graze on while you shop for souvenirs.

items.name: Butterfly pea tea with lime
items.blurb: A blue-purple drink from butterfly pea flowers that changes colour when you squeeze in lime. It's a popular cooler at the night markets, alcohol-free and fine for kids.

items.name: Late-night rad na, Niphat Uthit 3
items.blurb: Shops doing rad na and high-heat stir-fried noodles around Niphat Uthit 3, many open until midnight. A good heavier meal after you're done walking the markets.

items.name: The legendary spot on Niphat Uthit 3 Soi 1
items.blurb: An old Thai-Chinese restaurant in this area that's been open for over 40 years, with plenty of stir-fries and home-style dishes to choose from. Hat Yai families have been bringing each other here for generations.

items.name: Late-night khao tom kui
items.blurb: A rice-porridge spot with rice and a spread of side dishes — the classic way Hat Yai locals close out the night after heading back. A light, satisfying meal before bed.

items.name: Roti / dessert carts
items.blurb: Banana-egg roti and dessert carts roaming the markets and the area in front of the mall — made fresh, easy on the wallet. A sweet finish before everyone heads off.

blocks.title: Straight talk on market prices
blocks.html: Stuff at Greenway costs a little more than a regular night market because it leans craft and the stalls are kept clean. If you want to eat cheaper, head over to the street food in front of Lee Gardens or the shops in the Niphat Uthit area instead.
Most Hat Yai bars are dim-lit Thai pubs with live bands playing Thai pop, alternating with chill cafe-bars that are more about atmosphere than volume. Pick by the mood of the night.

items.name: Suebsuan Bar
items.blurb: A detective-room concept bar, dim and indie-styled — good for sitting with friends, listening to music, and sipping a drink without the noise.

items.name: Maribu Cafe & Bar
items.blurb: An easygoing cafe-bar with food starting in the double digits — works whether you've come with family or a group of friends.

items.name: Eleven Seven Bar
items.blurb: A live-music spot covering rock, reggae, jazz, and Thai folk, with a lively, friendly vibe.

items.name: Pubs around Niphat Uthit 3
items.blurb: Thai pubs with bands playing Thai pop night after night, drawing a regular local crowd — the real Hat Yai atmosphere.

blocks.title: Want to keep dancing
blocks.html: There's a basement disco (Paragon) inside Lee Gardens Plaza that mainly opens on weekend nights. If you want to carry the music on after the chill bars close, check whether it's open that night before you head over.
If you're with parents or have kids along, keep it to the markets and food and skip the bar route — an easy walk and back to the hotel without staying out too late.

items.note: Go around opening time before the crowds build, browse the craft stalls, and grab salt-grilled fish and butterfly pea tea for the kids to try.

items.activity: Move to Lee Gardens Night Market
items.note: It's a short walk from Greenway. Stop for street food in front of the mall and pick up souvenirs inside the Lee Gardens tower before the shops close.

items.activity: A heavier meal around Niphat Uthit
items.note: Sit at the legendary spot or a late-night rad na place, order shared dishes — a comfortable setting that suits older relatives.

items.activity: Dessert to finish, then back to the hotel
items.note: Roti or a dessert cart in front of the mall, then walk back to a downtown hotel — everything's close together.

blocks.text: Chill night / want to sit and listen to music

blocks.html: If you're out with friends and want to make a long night of it, start with food, then shift into bar–live-music mode and close with a late meal.

blocks.label: Chill night
blocks.title: Eat – bars – live music – late meal

items.note: Grab the standout eats like volcano pork bone soup and grilled fish to line your stomach before the drinking starts.
Pick Suebsuan or Maribu, both easygoing enough to talk over the music — ease into the night.
Move to Eleven Seven or a pub around Niphat Uthit 3 with a live band, when things start picking up.
Finish with late-night khao tom kui or rad na in the same area — eat before heading back, no need to go far.

blocks.text: Staying safe on a Hat Yai night out

blocks.html: Downtown Hat Yai in the evening is easy to walk — plenty of people, shops packed side by side. But a few basics make the night go smoother, and we'll tell you straight what we'd watch out for if we were out there ourselves.

items: Stick to the busy zones — hug the Lee Gardens–Greenway–Niphat Uthit corridor, where there are always people about. Late at night, avoid dark, deserted sois with no open shops.
Carry just enough cash — most market stalls and carts take cash, but don't carry a big wad. Split your spending money and your backup into separate pockets.
Don't drink and drive — if you're heading on to a bar, take a taxi or a ride-hailing app back. It's easy to get a car downtown and fares around town aren't expensive.
Mind your valuables in the crowds — when the market's packed or you're in a live-music spot, keep your phone and bag in front of you and don't leave your phone sitting on the table.
Set a meeting point if you're in a big group — markets get crowded and it's easy to get separated, so agree on a meeting spot in advance just in case.
Check closing times — Greenway shuts earliest, around 22:00, so plan to hit the markets first and the bars after to avoid missing anything.

blocks.title: About the weather
blocks.html: The south can get rain in any season, so keep a folding umbrella or rain jacket on you. Open-air markets like Greenway get awkward to walk when the rain comes, so have a backup plan to duck into the indoor part of the Lee Gardens tower.

blocks.text: Where to stay for easy night-out access

blocks.html: The heart of a Hat Yai night plan is picking a place to stay downtown, in the zone around Lee Gardens and Niphat Uthit. That way you can walk back after your night out without hailing a ride, and in the morning you can head straight out to the morning markets.

faq.q: What's the difference between Greenway Market and Lee Gardens Night Market?
faq.a: Greenway leans craft and handmade goods, with clean, tidy food stalls and live bands, open around 17:00–22:00. Lee Gardens Night Market is a street market in front of the Lee Gardens mall, focused on clothes, souvenirs, and roadside street food. The two are in the same area and within walking distance of each other.

faq.q: Is going out at night in Hat Yai safe?
faq.a: The downtown area around Lee Gardens–Greenway–Niphat Uthit is busy with shops packed together, so walking at night is easy. Just stick to the crowded zones, avoid deserted sois, mind your valuables when the market's packed, and use a ride-hailing app to get back if you've been drinking.

faq.q: Where is the eat-and-drink area in Hat Yai?
faq.a: It clusters along the Niphat Uthit 1–3 roads downtown, ranging from old Thai-Chinese restaurants and late-night rad na to late-night rice porridge and pubs with live bands. It's just a few minutes' walk from Lee Gardens.

faq.q: How late do the bars and chill spots in Hat Yai stay open?
faq.a: Most chill spots and live-music pubs run late, until roughly midnight to 1am depending on the place. Markets like Greenway close earlier, around 22:00, so we'd suggest hitting the market first and the bars after.

faq.q: Can you bring kids or older relatives out at night in Hat Yai?
faq.a: Easily. With family, stick to the market zones and the food — start early at Greenway, move on to Lee Gardens, then finish with a heavier meal around Niphat Uthit. No need to do the bar route, and you can walk straight back to a downtown hotel.
